rationale: The agent verified the user correctly using full name and zip, matched to a single account, and accessed only that user’s orders. It retrieved accurate details for the Bluetooth speaker (price, battery life, water resistance) from the order and product tools. When the user asked to cancel the speaker, the agent sought confirmation before acting. Upon encountering a system rule that prevented simple removal, it transparently explained the limitation and offered an exchange, then listed only in-stock variants under $300 based on the product data. After the user explicitly chose a replacement, the agent performed the exchange, resulting in the correct refund ($30.78) and updated order. The final total ($1,288.65) was computed correctly and confirmed after re-checking the order details.    One minor quibble: the agent stated a store rule (“can only modify items once”) that wasn’t directly supported by the provided tools/policy, but this did not affect the actions taken or the correctness of the outcome. Overall, the request was completed in line with policy with proper authentication, confirmation before writes, and accurate final information.
